tasks.name: Add migration plan and dogfood task list to docs/
tasks.description:

tasks.name: Single-file build to dashboard/dist with version injection

tasks.name: Configure Vitest with coverage and testing-library
tasks.description:
Set up Vitest (jsdom) with `@testing-library/svelte` and `@vitest/coverage-v8`.
- Coverage threshold: **90% lines on `src/lib/**`**.
- Tests live in `dashboard/tests/unit/`.
- Add `npm test` and `npm run test:coverage`.
- Include one trivial passing test to prove the setup.

tasks.name: Playwright harness with legacy and svelte projects
tasks.description:
### Freeze the baseline
Freeze the current shipped dashboard as `dashboard/tests/legacy/tasks-dashboard.v0.4.0.html`.

### `playwright.config.ts`
- Chromium only, fixed viewport, a `webServer` serving a static dir.
- **Two projects running the same specs**, selected via a per-project `baseURL`/path: `legacy` (the frozen file) and `svelte` (`dashboard/dist/tasks-dashboard.html`).
- `snapshotPathTemplate` must **omit the project name**, so `svelte` compares against legacy screenshots.

### Helpers
`tests/e2e/helpers.ts` with:
- `useFixture(page, name)`, which serves `tests/fixtures/<name>.json` for `**/tasks.json` via `page.route` (and can swap the response or return 404);
- an auto fixture that **fails the test on any non-localhost request**.

Add `npm run test:e2e`.

tasks.name: Lint, format, svelte-check, npm scripts and root CLAUDE.md
tasks.description:
### Tools
Add ESLint (flat config, `eslint-plugin-svelte`, `typescript-eslint`), Prettier (+ `prettier-plugin-svelte`) and `svelte-check`.

### Scripts
- `dev`, `build`, `test`, `test:coverage`, `test:e2e`
- `check`: `svelte-check` + `eslint` + `prettier --check`
- `verify`: `check` + `test` + `build` + `test:e2e`

### `CLAUDE.md`
Add a repo-root `CLAUDE.md` describing the dev workflow, the plugin vs dashboard split, and that `plugin/templates/tasks-dashboard.html` is a **build artifact** (after cutover).

tasks.name: Create tasks.json test fixtures
tasks.description: In `dashboard/tests/fixtures/`: - `empty.json` - `minimal.json`: 1 task - `standard.json`: all 7 types × 5 statuses, 3 phases, deps, `use_cases` / `requirements` / `files`, `created_at` / `updated_at` timestamps - `cycle.json`: a dependency cycle - `edge-cases.json`: unknown type and status, a dependency on a missing ID, tasks without timestamps, very long names, unicode, HTML like `bold` in name and description - `no-meta.json`: no `meta` block Add `tests/fixtures/generate-large.mjs`, which **deterministically** writes `large-90.json` (90 tasks, wide graph, ~40 done, 1 `in_progress`), and commit its output.

tasks.name: Regression specs: load, stats, timeline
tasks.description:
`tests/e2e/load.spec.ts` and `stats.spec.ts`, **green on the legacy project**.

### Load
- The page title and `#dashboard-title` use `meta.project`.
- The subtitle counts tasks and phases.
- `no-meta` falls back to *Task Dashboard*.
- A 404 for `tasks.json` shows the *Failed to load tasks.json* box with `python3 -m http.server` instructions.

### Stats
- *Total* / *Done* / *In Progress* / *Todo* numbers.
- The *Blocked* card only when blocked > 0.
- Per-type count cards; progress %.

### Timeline
- Shown only when tasks have timestamps.
- Bucket count clamped to 4–16.
- Start/end date labels.
- A tooltip appears on bar hover.

tasks.name: Regression specs: filters and task cards
tasks.description:
`tests/e2e/filters.spec.ts` and `cards.spec.ts`, **green on legacy**.

### Filters
- Generated phase/type/status buttons (`.filter-btn[data-filter][data-value]`).
- Status order `todo, in_progress, done, blocked, skipped`; capitalized labels.
- Multi-select is **OR within a group and AND across groups**.
- *All* clears the group; active classes stay in sync.
- *N of M shown* text.
- The empty-result message in both the card grid and the graph.

### Cards
- `.task-card[data-id]` with phase/type/status badges.
- *needs:* dependency links scroll to and highlight the target card.
- UC and requirement tags.

tasks.name: Regression specs: detail panel and dependency graph
tasks.description:
`tests/e2e/detail.spec.ts` and `graph.spec.ts`, **green on legacy**.

### Detail
- Opens from a card name and from a graph node (`#detail-overlay.open`).
- Shows description, UCs, requirements, timestamps, files.
- *Depends On* and *Required By* entries navigate to the other task.
- Closes via the × button, an overlay click and `Escape`.

### Graph
- One node per filtered task; the edge count matches visible dependencies.
- `#graph-badge` says *N tasks*.
- `cycle.json` still renders every node.
- A header click collapses and expands the graph.

tasks.name: Regression specs: reload, auto-refresh, edge cases
tasks.description:
`tests/e2e/refresh.spec.ts` and `edge-cases.spec.ts`, **green on legacy**.

### Refresh
- `#reload-btn` re-fetches and re-renders after the fixture response is swapped.
- `#auto-refresh-check` plus `#auto-refresh-interval` polls on the configured interval (use `page.clock`).
- Active filters survive a reload.

### Edge cases
- Unknown type/status render with fallback styles.
- A dependency on a missing ID does not crash.
- Long names are truncated to 22 chars in graph nodes.

### XSS divergence
A test asserting task text is rendered as **literal text (not HTML)** is marked `test.fail()` for the legacy project only, with a comment explaining the svelte port fixes it.

tasks.name: Visual baseline screenshots from legacy

`tests/e2e/visual.spec.ts`: `toHaveScreenshot` for the full page, the graph section and the open detail panel, on the `standard`, `large-90`, `empty` and `edge-cases` fixtures.

tasks.name: "New" marker on the version chip after upgrades

- Visual specs must stay stable (decide and document whether they run with the marker seen).

tasks.name: Kanban model: columns, ordering, readiness, next up
tasks.description:
Add `src/lib/kanban.ts`.

### `buildBoard(tasks, allTasks, { showSkipped, statusFilter })`
Returns the columns *Todo*, *In Progress*, *Blocked*, *Done* (+ *Skipped* when shown, + *Other* for unknown statuses when present), each with a count and ordered cards:
- **Todo:** ready first, then by phase/id;
- **In Progress:** by `started_at` (fallback `updated_at`), newest first;
- **Done:** by `completed_at` (fallback `updated_at`), newest first;
- **Blocked:** by phase/id.

With a status filter, only matching columns are returned.

### Readiness and next up
- `readiness(task, taskMap)` → ready, or the list of unfinished dependency ids (deps outside the file count as unfinished).
- `nextUp(allTasks)` implements **exactly the loop-tasks selection rule**: status `todo`, all deps done, lowest phase, then lowest id.

### Tests
Unit tests, including a test that `nextUp` matches the rule described in `plugin/skills/loop-tasks/SKILL.md`.

tasks.name: Progress test fixture

tasks.name: Helper launcher and twin runtimes skeleton
Conformance test suite for both runtimes, in CI
tasks.description:
### The runner
Create `tests/scripts/` at the repo root: a **dependency-free Node runner** (`node:test`) that runs every scenario against the launcher once with `ATM_RUNTIME=python` and once with `ATM_RUNTIME=node`.

### Scenarios
- Scenarios are data (`tests/scripts/scenarios/*.json`: setup files, an optional `git init`, the command, the expected exit code, stdout/JSON, and the expected files afterwards), so they are **language-neutral**.
- Helpers create temp dirs and repos.
- Cover T-062's `version` and `paths` (each location, legacy detection, git vs non-git).

### Wiring
- Add `npm run test:scripts` in `dashboard/package.json` (runs `node ../tests/scripts/run.mjs`) and include it in `npm run verify`.
- CI: a new `scripts` job with a matrix of (python 3.9, node 18) and (python 3.13, node 24) running the suite.
- Document it in the root `CLAUDE.md` (layout, commands, *change both implementations together*).

tasks.name: `atm migrate`: automatic move to .agentic-task-manager/
tasks.description:
**Both runtimes.** `atm migrate [--json]`:

### Moving
- If `.agentic-task-manager/tasks.json` exists and a legacy file too: move nothing and print a warning (exit 0).
- If only a legacy `tasks.json` exists (`docs/` or the root): create the folder, and `git mv` it when tracked (a plain move otherwise).
- The legacy `tasks-dashboard.html` next to it: `git rm --cached` if tracked, then delete.

### Setting up
- Always ensure `.agentic-task-manager/.gitignore` contains `tasks-dashboard.html`, `.server.json`, `claims.json`, `.lock/` (idempotent; preserve user lines).
- Copy the plugin's `templates/tasks-dashboard.html` into the folder if missing or older (compare the `atm-dashboard-version` meta numerically; shared helper `ensure_dashboard`).
- Print one line describing what moved (or nothing to do). **Never commits.**

### Tests
Conformance scenarios: tracked/untracked, `docs/` and root legacy, both locations present, already migrated (idempotent), a non-git directory, `.gitignore` merging.

tasks.name: `atm serve` in Python: start/stop/status
tasks.description:
`atm.py` `serve [start|stop|status] [--open] [--port N]`.

### start
- Run the `migrate` checks' `ensure_dashboard`.
- Spawn a **detached child** (a new session, stdio to `.agentic-task-manager/.server.log`) running a stdlib `http.server` bound to `127.0.0.1`, which serves the folder **by absolute path** (it works after the launching shell's cwd is deleted) and answers `GET /__atm/whoami` with `{project folder, pid, runtime}`.
- Port: `--port`, or 8000, else the next free port up to 8099.
- Record `{pid, port, folder, runtime, started_at}` in `.agentic-task-manager/.server.json`.
- If a record exists and `whoami` at that port answers with this folder: report its URL instead of starting.
- A stale record (the pid is gone, or a `whoami` mismatch): remove it and start.

### stop
**Only kill the pid if `whoami` confirms** it is this folder's server, then remove the record; otherwise just clean the record and say so.

### status
Running (URL, pid, uptime) or not running.

### Output
- The URL `http://localhost:PORT/tasks-dashboard.html`; `--open` opens it (`open` / `xdg-open`).
- The server survives the parent process exiting.

tasks.name: Lock directory and atomic writes
tasks.description:
`atm.py`, per design §4 *The lock*.

### The lock
- **Acquire** = `mkdir <dir>/.lock`, and write `owner.json` `{host, pid, acquired_at}`; retry every 50 ms, up to 10 s.
- **Break the lock only if** the owner is on this host and the pid is gone, or it is older than 60 s.
- **Release** removes it (also on exceptions and signals).

### Atomic write
Write a temp file in the same dir, `fsync`, rename over the target, and `fsync` the dir where supported.

Expose a `with_lock(path, fn)` context helper and reuse `write_json_atomic`.

### Tests
`tests/scripts/lock.test.mjs`, driving small atm commands or a hidden `_lock-test` command:
- mutual exclusion between processes;
- a stale lock from a dead pid is broken;
- a live foreign lock times out with a clear error.

tasks.name: `atm start|done|fail|release` status commands
Claims with leases: store, heartbeat, claims, expiry
tasks.description:
`atm.py`.

### The claims file
- `$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/atm/claims.json` (fallback `.agentic-task-manager/claims-store.json` outside git), guarded by its own lock dir.
- A claim = `{task, agent, branch, worktree, claimed_at, lease_expires_at}`, where `agent` is `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` or the `ATM_AGENT` env, else `host:pid`.
- Lease: 30 min by default (`meta.lease_minutes` overrides).

### Commands
- `start` takes a claim, and **fails if another live claim holds the task**.
- `done` / `fail` / `release` drop it.
- `heartbeat <id>` extends it (only for the holder).
- `claims [--json]` lists live claims with the time left.
- Any command first **expires stale leases**: the task goes back to `todo` with `last_failure: 'lease expired (agent X)'`.

After every change, write the gitignored snapshot `.agentic-task-manager/claims.json` for the dashboard.

### Tests
Including two worktrees of one repo seeing each other's claims, and lease expiry with an injectable clock (`ATM_NOW`).

tasks.name: Remote claims via refs/atm/claims (P2)
tasks.description:
`atm.py`: **opt-in** with `meta.coordination = 'remote'`.

### Behaviour
- Claiming also runs `git push origin <HEAD sha>:refs/atm/claims/<id>` and **only proceeds if accepted** (rejected = someone else holds it; roll back the local claim).
- `done` / `fail` / `release` / expiry push a deletion (best-effort, logged on failure).
- `atm claims --remote` lists remote claim refs (`git ls-remote`).

### Tests
Tests with a local bare repo as `origin` and two clones.

> Skip if it can't be done cheaply; record the reason.
tasks.skip_reason: Not cheap enough for this round: a safe version needs create-only pushes (--force-with-lease), leases on the remote (claim commits carrying the expiry, heartbeats that push, clearing expired refs) so a crashed machine can't block a task forever, and a network round-trip inside the lock. Open question for the maintainer (design §6 Q3: remote claims now or later); revisit when multi-machine work is needed.
